$schema_note: VIGIL feature-wiring completeness audit (W15-2 #394, feeding the W17 milestone). Machine-checked by docs/tests/test_feature_wiring_status.py, which runs in the required 'the briefing explains every agent and capability' CI job. JSON, not YAML, on purpose: that job installs only pytest. Every feature carries a machine-readable wiring status; the guard verifies each status against the code and EXTENDS the system-map drift invariant with three set-equality/AST coverage checks: (1) the CLI surface (native verbs == sub.add_parser set; passthrough verbs == the dispatch _ENV table); (2) the UI surface (the declared ui-screen set == the app.js NAV ids == the app.js route() ids, reusing tools/system-map/generate.py's own extraction); and (3) the subsystem seams (chat, fireteam, brain, the MCP tool-governance boundary, and the not-yet-wired MCP live-client seam), each anchored to a real AST symbol. So no verb, screen, or subsystem seam can be silently added, removed, or mis-declared. See docs/features/wiring-status.md.

statuses.LIVE: Shipped and unconditionally invokable; produces its effect on the default path.
statuses.OPT-IN: Shipped but off by default; the operator turns it on explicitly.
statuses.GATED: Shipped but its effect is behind an authorization/approval/quorum gate or is deploy-gated on infra.
statuses.BUILT-NOT-WIRED: The symbol exists (interface/stub/scaffold) but no runtime reaches it; a stub raises NotImplementedError or a scaffold is an abstract interface only.
statuses.ORPHANED: A registered surface (e.g. a console read route) that nothing consumes; detection is enforced by the W17-14 orphan-route guard. No feature is ORPHANED today.

features.name: Homegrown decision brain (vigil engage --brain hexstrike)
features.rationale: Off by default: `--brain` defaults to "" (cli.py add_argument choices ('', 'hexstrike')); passing `--brain hexstrike` drives `think` with the drift-free, propose-only planner. The gate + governed executor + oracle are unchanged (the brain only proposes).

features.name: Command-UI chat orchestrator (/api/chat/send)
features.rationale: The agentic chat operator behind the `chat` UI screen; wired into the console API at POST /api/chat/send (console/server.py). Every action it launches routes the SAME gate/oracle/two-env boundary as a CLI engage.

features.name: Fireteam multi-agent fan-out (run_fireteam)
features.rationale: Wired into the live engine via live/wiring.py's `deploy_fireteam`, but only on an APPROVED deploy decision: members are capped, reuse the parent's gate/oracle (never a privileged copy), and run_fireteam validates the plan fail-closed (a malformed / over-cap / mutex plan spawns nothing).

features.name: Sovereign MCP tool-call boundary (authorize_tool_call)
features.rationale: Every tool call is subordinated to the sovereign core: the manifest phase maps onto the WARDEN tier, a destructive tool floors at A3 + the m-of-n leg, and the whole thing routes through the injected conjunctive gate. Reached at runtime by live/executor.py and the fireteam members (fail-closed).

features.name: Live external-MCP-server client (the manifest's consumer)
features.rationale: The pluggable MCP-server MANIFEST layer is built and validated (least-privilege phases, fail-closed cross-server validation, secret redaction) and to_client_config produces the transport config a live client would consume — but NO runtime consumes it: the client that actually speaks to an MCP server is a later slice (see the module docstring). test_mcp_live_client_seam_is_still_unwired asserts to_client_config has zero runtime call-sites, so wiring it forces this status off BUILT-NOT-WIRED. W17 milestone item.

features.name: vigil escrow-passphrase
features.rationale: W7-7 optional m-of-n passphrase escrow; off by default, run explicitly to split the backup passphrase into shares.

features.name: vigil recover-passphrase
features.rationale: W7-7 recovery half; reconstruct an escrowed backup passphrase from a threshold set of share files (fail-closed below threshold).

features.name: vigil fireteam
features.rationale: W17-7 #541 Tier-B escalation resolve loop (list|approve|resolve): the operator signs an owner approval for an over-cap fireteam member escalation and the offense resolver applies the registry's signed-only resolve() — owner-key gated; without a signed approval an escalation still auto-rejects at its deadline (fail-closed).

features.name: UI target-authorization ceremony (add + owner-sign a live external target)
features.rationale: Phase 1.b. Owner-gated (do_action target_add -> PERMISSION_BY_ACTION offense_authority, owner-only): the cockpit owner-signs a scoped, time-boxed, GET-only-by-default EngagementAuthority IN-PROCESS and writes only the public signed bundle to the .vigil-live seam (the owner private key never leaves the sovereign process). Refuses a categorical-safety-floor host, a loopback/link-local/metadata IP, and a live environment. list/status are read-only.

features.name: Offense-side install of a UI-authorized live target
features.rationale: Phase 1.c. On a remote launch, reads the seam bundle and installs it ONLY when it is tied to the PINNED owner key, its signature verifies, its window is current, and its scope entries are bare hosts; refuses to downgrade a differing/unreadable trust root. Then the launch gate _has_verified_authority(slug, host) additionally requires the verified authority's scope to cover the target host. Honest bound (docs/limitations): the owner anchor + launch-gate authority root live under the offense-writable root; anchor .authority-root out-of-band (VIGIL_AUTHORITY_ROOT_DIR read-only/HSM) to close a full-FS-write attacker.

features.name: Operator rate / User-Agent controls (B10)
features.rationale: Phase 3 / B10. The scanner ALWAYS identifies itself (correlatable OBSIDIAN UA) and throttles per the charter posture; these OPT-IN controls (env VIGIL_OPERATOR_ID + VIGIL_MIN_REQUEST_INTERVAL_S, threaded by console.actions._operator_traffic_controls and surfaced read-only as launch_assessment's traffic_profile) let the operator tag the UA and set a rate FLOOR that can only TIGHTEN the posture rate (max(posture_floor, operator_min)), never loosen it. Off by default (posture rate + base UA); claim PHASE3-1.

features.name: AEGIS gateway external verdict sink (P4)
features.rationale: Phase 4. The gateway always streams verdicts to the UI/stderr; `aegis gateway --verdict-webhook URL [--verdict-sink webhook|slack]` (and console aegis_setup body verdict_webhook/verdict_sink) ADDITIONALLY POSTs each verdict to an operator SIEM/webhook/Slack via the bounded, redirects-disabled report.push.push_via_urllib. Off by default. Browser-safe body (no oracle-context), auth from AEGIS_VERDICT_WEBHOOK_AUTHORIZATION env (not argv), fail-open (never perturbs the data plane); notification only — orthogonal to the AEGIS_RESPOND+kill-switch enforcement gate. Claim PHASE4-1.
